chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: How "Tanga" came about
summary: Machito says Mario was wrong that he was there; "Tanga" grew from a vamp behind Miguelito's "Botellero" by pianist Varona and Mario's melody.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: John Bartee's arrangement, eh?, and not long after that is when Afro-Cuban jazz was born. Now, I made a mistake, I thought that Afro-Cuban was invented while you were in the service, but Mario Bauza says that you were there at the rehearsals when it was thought of. What do you remember about "Tanga"?
Well, Mario made a mistake. I came after the "Tanga" was made.

....because they was accompanying Miguelito Valdes in "Botellero" - bran-baran-bam - a sort of vamp or botellero. Varona was the piano player in that particular time. You know, sometime you fake, you start to vamp and to filling in two minutes or three minutes because of the show
time or whatever, so he started baran-bam - baran-bam; Mario start to give it a broken chord to the saxophone and him with the trumpet and then after sometime Mario create the melody on top of .....
